error_model: Qorvo DWM3000 (MATLAB waveform simulation, tunnel channel)
error_model_scope: Bootstrap over 3600 waveform-level ranging trials simulated in MATLAB for DWM3000 at 499.200 MHz bandwidth, conditions TUNNEL. Error comes from the transmitted waveform, a cluster-based multipath channel and the signal-to-noise ratio, through a leading-edge or peak time-of-arrival estimator. Nothing here was measured on hardware: the channel parameters follow the shape of the IEEE 802.15.4a models but are this project's, and the estimator is a reference implementation rather than any vendor's.
error_model_caveats: Constant offset of -0.38 m removed; per-unit ranging calibration is what takes that out in a deployment.

evidence.source_name: Practical DWM3000 range reports, upper half of the band
evidence.source_scope: Qorvo publishes no maximum range for the DWM3000. Reported practical figures span roughly 50-100 m for commercial modules in ordinary use, against 300 m advertised for the DWM1000 predecessor and 500 m demonstrated on DW3000 boards with external antennas in clear line of sight.
evidence.caveats: 150 m sits in the upper half of the practical band, on the argument that a tunnel bore guides the signal instead of letting it spread spherically. This is the single most consequential assumption in the study: it decides whether the report's own 150 m node spacing can produce a fix at all.
